st.yv.bali_same_days.l: When life feels like a loop, the work is not more of it but mastering the mind that runs it.
st.yv.bali_same_days.s: The demon king Bali has ruled the three worlds for ages. One day at his window he realises he is doing the same things day after day, night after night, and asks what any of it adds up to. He remembers a riddle his father Virochana once told him: a vast realm ruled by a silent king and an all-powerful minister. The minister is the mind; win it over, by practice, and everything is won.
st.yv.bali_same_days.t: Bali tires of endless days and asks his father's riddle

st.yv.bhasa_vilasa_old_friends.l: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.
st.yv.bhasa_vilasa_old_friends.s: Bhasa and Vilasa grow up inseparable in a forest hermitage. After their fathers die they drift apart and spend long lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well; he answers honestly that there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks and worries.
st.yv.bhasa_vilasa_old_friends.t: Two old friends meet again and admit they never found peace

st.yv.bhushunda_the_old_crow.l: A long, steady life comes from a mind that stays in the present, wants little and stays kind.
st.yv.bhushunda_the_old_crow.s: Vasishtha travels to a wish-fulfilling tree on Mount Meru to meet Bhushunda, a crow who has watched world-ages come and go. Asked how he has lived so long, untroubled, Bhushunda lists his habits: he doesn't brood on the past or future, doesn't fret about what he'll get next, doesn't grow arrogant from knowing, and shares in others' joys and sorrows.
st.yv.bhushunda_the_old_crow.t: Bhushunda, the crow who outlived the ages

st.yv.janaka_overhears_the_siddhas.l: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
st.yv.janaka_overhears_the_siddhas.s: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
st.yv.janaka_overhears_the_siddhas.t: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind

st.yv.karunya_stops_acting.l: Don't freeze while you wait to be sure. Understanding and action have to fly together.
st.yv.karunya_stops_acting.s: A student asks the sage Agastya whether freedom comes from action or from knowledge. Agastya answers with a story: young Karunya, confused by two scriptures, simply stopped doing anything, and his father had to show him that understanding and action work together.
st.yv.karunya_stops_acting.t: Karunya stops acting: knowledge and action as two wings

st.yv.prahlada_refuge_in_victor.l: Refuge is open to anyone, whatever their past; devotion kept up daily changes the mind.
st.yv.prahlada_refuge_in_victor.s: With his father killed and his people beaten, the young demon prince Prahlada sees no way out except to take refuge in the very god he feared. He worships Vishnu in mind and in his shrine; the gods doubt a demon can be devoted, but Vishnu tells them he is ready. Vishnu appears, Prahlada sings a hymn of refuge, sinks into realisation and is gently woken to rule with a steady mind.
st.yv.prahlada_refuge_in_victor.t: Prahlada, alone after defeat, takes refuge in Narayana

st.yv.prahlada_woken_to_rule.l: Grace and effort work together; keep practising daily, and let the mind ripen slowly.
st.yv.prahlada_woken_to_rule.s: After telling how Prahlada awakened, Vasishtha faces Rama's challenge: if everything comes by effort, wasn't Prahlada saved by Vishnu's grace? Vasishtha answers that Prahlada earned it himself, that the Self and Vishnu are not two, and that sometimes we wake by our own effort and sometimes by grace reached through devotion. Steady daily practice ripens the mind like a mango.
st.yv.prahlada_woken_to_rule.t: Prahlada: effort and grace are not rivals

st.yv.punya_consoles_pavana.l: Grief is love; endless rumination is the part we can learn to stop feeding.
st.yv.punya_consoles_pavana.s: Two brothers live with their parents by the Ganga. When their father and mother die, the elder, Punya, performs the rites calmly while the younger, Pavana, wanders the forest weeping. Punya gently helps him see that the bonds of 'mine' and 'not mine' are made in the mind. Vasishtha draws the lesson: worry grows when fed, and a full mind finds the world full.
st.yv.punya_consoles_pavana.t: Punya consoles his younger brother Pavana after their parents die

st.yv.rama_stops_eating_after_pilgrimage.l: Losing interest in everything can be the start of asking better questions, if someone helps you through it.
st.yv.rama_stops_eating_after_pilgrimage.s: Sixteen-year-old Rama returns from a long pilgrimage and quietly withdraws: he stops eating properly, stops laughing, ignores his duties and sits alone. His attendants tell the worried king. Vishvamitra and Vasishtha say this is not illness or weakness but the first stirring of real questions, and ask that Rama be brought to them.
st.yv.rama_stops_eating_after_pilgrimage.t: Rama comes home from his pilgrimage and loses interest in everything

st.yv.vasishtha_effort_over_fate.l: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.
st.yv.vasishtha_effort_over_fate.s: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
st.yv.vasishtha_effort_over_fate.t: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort

yv.1.1.7.m: Just as birds fly through the sky on both their wings, the highest state is reached through both knowledge and action.
roles: Shows seeing the two as one flight.
yv.1.1.7.sa: उभाभ्यामेव पक्षाभ्यां यथा खे पक्षिणां गतिः । तथैव ज्ञानकर्मभ्यां जायते परमं पदम् ॥

yv.1.10.9.m: Ever since lotus-eyed Rama came back from his pilgrimage with the brahmins, he has been low in spirit.
roles: A change others notice before he can explain it.
yv.1.10.9.sa: रामो राजीवपत्राक्षो यतःप्रभृति चागतः । सविप्रस्तीर्थयात्रायास्ततःप्रभृति दुर्मनाः ॥

scene.s: Sixteen-year-old Rama returns from a long pilgrimage and quietly withdraws: he stops eating properly, stops laughing, ignores his duties and sits alone. His attendants tell the worried king. Vishvamitra and Vasishtha say this is not illness or weakness but the first stirring of real questions, and ask that Rama be brought to them.
scene.t: Rama comes home from his pilgrimage and loses interest in everything

yv.1.11.37.m: Say quickly whatever you wish, blameless one, and you will have it, by which these sorrows will never pierce you again.
roles: Shows trust that there is someone to tell.
yv.1.11.37.sa: यथाभिमतमाशु त्वं ब्रूहि प्राप्स्यसि चानघ । सर्वमेव पुनर्येन भेत्स्यन्ते त्वां तु नाधयः ॥

scene.s: Vishvamitra gently invites the withdrawn Rama to speak.

yv.1.13.11.m: A wealthy man whom no one blames, a brave man who doesn't boast, and a man in power who treats all alike: these three are rare.
roles: Shows power joined to even regard.
yv.1.13.11.sa: श्रीमानजननिन्द्यश्च शूरश्चाप्यविकत्थनः । समदृष्टिः प्रभुश्चैव दुर्लभाः पुरुषास्त्रयः ॥

yv.1.13.8.m: People are cool and gentle to touch, with strangers and their own alike, only until wealth hardens them, as a blizzard hardens snow.
roles: Shows what prosperity does to tenderness.
yv.1.13.8.sa: तावच्छीतमृदुस्पर्शाः परे स्वे च जने जनाः । वात्ययेव हिमं यावच्छ्रिया न परुषीकृताः ॥

yv.1.14.10.m: That alone is called living by which one gains what is truly worth gaining, after which one does not grieve again: the place of highest peace.
roles: Names a measure for a life.
yv.1.14.10.sa: प्राप्यं संप्राप्यते येन भूयो येन न शोच्यते । पराया निर्वृतेः स्थानं यत्तज्जीवितमुच्यते ॥

yv.1.16.22.m: The mind swoops onto tasks like a bird onto meat, and a moment later loses interest, like a child with a toy.
roles: Shows keen starts and instant loss of interest.
yv.1.16.22.sa: चेतः पतति कार्येषु विहगः स्वामिषेष्विव । क्षणेन विरतिं याति बालः क्रीडनकादिव ॥

yv.1.16.25.m: The mind is the cause of all things; while it is active the three worlds exist, and when it fades the world fades. So it must be treated with care.
roles: Shows attention turning from circumstances to the mind that meets them.
yv.1.16.25.sa: चित्तं कारणमर्थानां तस्मिन्सति जगत्त्रयम् । तस्मिन्क्षीणे जगत्क्षीणं तच्चिकित्स्यं प्रयत्नतः ॥

yv.1.16.3.m: The mind never really gets anything anywhere; even when great riches come, it never fills up inside, like a wicker basket dipped in water.
roles: Shows getting more and still not feeling full.
yv.1.16.3.sa: न प्राप्नोति क्वचित्किंचित्प्राप्तैरपि महाधनैः । नान्तः संपूर्णतामेति करण्डक इवाम्बुभिः ॥

yv.1.17.14.m: Knotted inside the body and hard to cut, craving drags a person along the way a rope drags a bullock.
roles: Shows being pulled along by wanting one cannot cut.
yv.1.17.14.sa: अन्तर्ग्रथितया देहे सर्वदुश्छेदयाऽनया । रज्ज्वेवाशु बलीवर्दस्तृष्णया वाह्यते जनः ॥

yv.1.17.43.m: People let go of all their sorrow when they let go of worry. Giving up worry is called the cure for the sickness of craving.
roles: Shows letting a wanted thing go unrehearsed.
yv.1.17.43.sa: लोकोऽयमखिलं दुःखं चिन्तयोज्झितयोज्झति । तृष्णाविषूचिकामन्त्रश्चिन्तात्यागो हि कथ्यते ॥

yv.1.17.50.m: Even a man who is wise, brave and steady as Mount Meru, the best of men, craving alone turns into a blade of grass in an instant.
roles: Shows craving lowering anyone and being caught by it.
yv.1.17.50.sa: अपि मेरुसमं प्राज्ञमपि शूरमपि स्थिरम् । तृणीकरोति तृष्णैका निमेषेण नरोत्तमम् ॥

yv.1.26.11.m: Our own senses are the enemies; truth itself has turned untrue; the self strikes the self, and the mind is the mind's own enemy.
roles: Shows the sense of being one's own worst enemy.
yv.1.26.11.sa: शत्रवश्चेन्द्रियाण्येव सत्यं यातमसत्यताम् । प्रहरत्यात्मनैवात्मा मनसैव मनो रिपुः ॥

yv.1.26.21.m: Steadiness turns into unsteadiness, and people keep rising and falling; bad company is easy to find, good company is hard to find.
roles: Shows weariness at a world where nothing holds.
yv.1.26.21.sa: धीरताऽधीरतामेति पातोत्पातपरो जनः । सुलभो दुर्जनाश्लेषो दुर्लभः सत्समागमः ॥

yv.1.26.39.m: I think only the awakened person is happy: one whose mind is cool within, who works for others' good and is moved by their pain.
roles: Shows being moved by another's pain.
yv.1.26.39.sa: परोपकारकारिण्या परार्तिपरितप्तया । बुद्ध एव सुखी मन्ये स्वात्मशीतलया धिया ॥

yv.1.27.19.m: After roaming far and wide all day and coming home at evening, who sleeps at night when the day has been empty of the good work that wise people lean on?
roles: Shows lying awake after a busy day that held nothing of worth.
yv.1.27.19.sa: इतस्ततो दूरतरं विहृत्य प्रविश्य गेहं दिवसावसाने । विवेकिलोकाश्रयसाधुकर्म रिक्तेऽह्नि रात्रौ क उपैति निद्राम् ॥

yv.1.27.9.m: Those who cross the ocean of battle, with its waves of war elephants, are not heroes in my eyes. The real heroes cross this ocean of body and senses, with its waves of mind.
roles: Riding out the waves of the mind.
yv.1.27.9.sa: तरन्ति मातङ्गघटातरङ्गं रणाम्बुधिं ये मयि ते न शूराः । शूरास्त एवेह मनस्तरङ्गं देहेन्द्रियाम्भोधिमिमं तरन्ति ॥

yv.1.28.17.m: Those days, those great people, that wealth, those deeds: all have passed into memory. We too will go in a moment.
roles: Shows everything once solid as already memory.
yv.1.28.17.sa: दिवसास्ते महान्तस्ते संपदस्ताः क्रियाश्च ताः । सर्वं स्मृतिपथं यातं यामो वयमपि क्षणात् ॥

yv.1.29.22.m: Great sage, there are no troubles in the world that do not fade through the company of noble-minded people, as the darkness of night fades before the moon.
yv.1.29.22.sa: विद्यन्त एवेह न ते महात्मन् दुराधयो न क्षयमाप्नुवन्ति । ये सङ्गमेनोत्तममानसानां निशातमांसीव निशाकरेण ॥

yv.1.30.17.m: How can a person who lives and works in the middle of the world not be bound by it, the way water sits on a lotus leaf?
roles: Shows the wish to stay engaged and yet free.
yv.1.30.17.sa: संसार एव निवहे जनो व्यवहरन्नपि । न बन्धं कथमाप्नोति पद्मपत्रे पयो यथा ॥

yv.1.31.17.m: Tell me the skill by which sorrow doesn't come to me while I go about my work, or else tell me the best way of dealing with life itself.
roles: He asks for a workable way, not an escape.
yv.1.31.17.sa: व्यवहारवतो युक्त्या दुःखं नायाति मे यया । अथवा व्यवहारस्य ब्रूत तां युक्तिमुत्तमाम् ॥

yv.1.31.7.m: There is nothing on earth, or in heaven among the gods, so trivial that the wise cannot make it beautiful.
roles: A clear mind lends beauty to small things.
yv.1.31.7.sa: न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा क्वचित् । सुधियस्तुच्छमप्येतद्यन्नयन्ति न रम्यताम् ॥

yv.2.11.58.m: From constant contact with good people, discernment is born; and the fruits of the tree of discernment are both enjoyment and freedom.
yv.2.11.58.sa: नित्यं सज्जनसंपर्काद्विवेक उपजायते । विवेकपादपस्यैव भोगमोक्षौ फले स्मृतौ ॥

yv.2.13.53.m: For a person content in calm, clear and cool within, whose mind is adorned with peace, even an enemy becomes a friend.
roles: Shows hostility softens around a settled person.
yv.2.13.53.sa: पुंसः प्रशमतृप्तस्य शीतलाच्छतरात्मनः । शमभूषितचित्तस्य शत्रुरप्येति मित्रताम् ॥

yv.2.13.64.m: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, with a mind cooled by calm, tastes truly sweet; nothing else tastes so sweet to the heart.
yv.2.13.64.sa: यत्करोषि यदश्नासि शमशीतलया धिया । तत्रातिस्वदते स्वादु नेतरत्तात मानसे ॥

yv.2.13.67.m: One whose whole being is armoured in the nectar of calm is not pierced by sorrows, as arrows cannot pierce a diamond rock.
yv.2.13.67.sa: सुसंनद्धसमस्ताङ्गं प्रशमामृतवर्मणा । वेधयन्ति न दुःखानि शरा वज्रशिलामिव ॥

yv.2.13.72.m: One who hears, touches, sees, eats and smells things pleasant and unpleasant, and is neither elated nor dejected, is called calm.
yv.2.13.72.sa: श्रुत्वा स्पृष्ट्वा च दृष्ट्वा च भुक्त्वा घ्रात्वा शुभाशुभम् । न हृष्यति ग्लायति यः स शान्त इति कथ्यते ॥

yv.2.13.78.m: One who has become cool within, who does not drown in things, who is busy in the world yet not confused: such a person is called calm.
yv.2.13.78.sa: योऽन्तः शीतलतां यातो यो भावेषु न मज्जति । व्यवहारी न संमूढः स शान्त इति कथ्यते ॥

yv.2.14.11.m: Minds that have been opened by discernment do not sink in misfortune, just as gourds do not sink in water.
yv.2.14.11.sa: या विवेकविकासिन्यो मतयो महतामिह । न ता विपदि मज्जन्ति तुम्बकानीव वारिणि ॥

yv.2.14.2.m: Sharpened by inquiry, the mind sees the highest. Inquiry is the great medicine for the long illness of worldly life.
roles: Shows wanting to understand is honoured.
yv.2.14.2.sa: विचारात्तीक्ष्णतामेत्य धीः पश्यति परं पदम् । दीर्घसंसाररोगस्य विचारो हि महौषधम् ॥

yv.2.14.50.m: 'Who am I? How did this trouble called worldly life come upon me?' Reflecting on this rightly is called inquiry.
roles: The question who am I begins self-knowledge.
yv.2.14.50.sa: कोऽहं कथमयं दोषः संसाराख्य उपागतः । न्यायेनेति परामर्शो विचार इति कथ्यते ॥

yv.2.14.53.m: Through inquiry, truth is known; through truth, rest in oneself; from that comes a calm mind, and from that, the end of all sorrow.
roles: Shows the chain from inquiry to rest in oneself.
yv.2.14.53.sa: विचाराज्ज्ञायते तत्त्वं तत्त्वाद्विश्रान्तिरात्मनि । अतो मनसि शान्तत्वं सर्वदुःखपरिक्षयः ॥

yv.2.15.1.m: Contentment is the highest good; contentment is what is called happiness. The contented person reaches the deepest rest, O destroyer of foes.
roles: Names contentment as the highest good.
yv.2.15.1.sa: संतोषो हि परं श्रेयः संतोषः सुखमुच्यते संतुष्टः परमभ्येति विश्राममरिसूदन ॥

yv.2.15.11.m: Even a person who owns nothing enjoys the happiness of an emperor, if their mind is content and free of mental and bodily troubles.
yv.2.15.11.sa: अकिंचनोऽप्यसौ जन्तुः साम्राज्यसुखमश्नुते । आधिव्याधिविनिर्मुक्तं संतुष्टं यस्य मानसम् ॥

yv.2.15.19.m: People feel more joy looking at a face made beautiful by equanimity than from piles of wealth.
roles: Evenness shows and others are gladdened by it.
yv.2.15.19.sa: समतासुन्दरं वक्रं पुरुषस्यावलोकयन् । तोषमेति यथा लोको न तथा धनसंचयैः ॥

yv.2.16.19.m: Contentment is the greatest gain, good company the best path, inquiry the highest knowledge, and calm the greatest happiness.
yv.2.16.19.sa: संतोषः परमो लाभः सत्सङ्गः परमा गतिः । विचारः परमं ज्ञानं शमो हि परमं सुखम् ॥

yv.2.16.3.m: In the company of the wise, emptiness becomes fullness, even death feels like a festival, and misfortune looks like good fortune.
roles: Shows trust in the company of the wise.

yv.2.16.32.m: When one good quality grows, other good qualities grow and overcome faults; when one fault grows, faults grow and destroy good qualities.
roles: Cultivates starting with one good quality and the rest following.
yv.2.16.32.sa: गुणे विवृद्धे वर्धन्ते गुणा दोषजयप्रदाः । दोषे विवृद्धे वर्धन्ते दोषा गुणविनाशनाः ॥

yv.2.16.8.m: Even when people fall into the hardest straits and feel helpless, they should not let go of good company, not even a little.
roles: Holding to those who steady you.
yv.2.16.8.sa: अपि कष्टतरां प्राप्तैर्दशां विवशतां गतैः । मनागपि न संत्याज्या मानवैः साधुसंगतिः ॥

yv.2.4.12.m: Whoever wants something and works for it step by step will surely get it, unless they turn back halfway.
roles: Shows not turning back at the midpoint.
yv.2.4.12.sa: यो यमर्थं प्रार्थयते तदर्थं चेहते क्रमात् । अवश्यं स तमाप्नोति न चेदर्धान्निवर्तते ॥

yv.2.5.12.m: There is no doubt: past faults are calmed by present virtues. The proof is that yesterday's mistake is undone by today's good deeds.
yv.2.5.12.sa: दोषः शाम्यत्यसंदेहं प्राक्तनोऽद्यतनैर्गुणैः । दृष्टान्तोऽत्र ह्यस्तनस्य दोषस्याद्य गुणैः क्षयः ॥

yv.2.5.20.m: 'Fate is pushing me': that is what burnt-out minds say. Seeing those who look only to the unseen, good fortune turns away.
roles: Shows fate as an excuse being taken away.
yv.2.5.20.sa: दैवं संप्रेरयति मामिति दग्धधियां मुखम् । अदृष्टश्रेष्ठदृष्टीनां दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मीर्निवर्तते ॥

scene.s: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
scene.t: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort

yv.2.5.30.m: If there were no laziness in the world, who would not be rich or learned? It is through laziness that this earth, to its ocean shores, is full of people as dull as cattle, and poor.
roles: Names sloth as the great waste.
yv.2.5.30.sa: आलस्यं यदि न भवेज्जगत्यनर्थः को न स्याद्बहुधनको बहुश्रुतो वा । आलस्यादियमवनिः ससागरान्ता संपूर्णा नरपशुभिश्च निर्धनैश्च ॥

scene.s: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
scene.t: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort

yv.2.5.5.m: Past effort and present effort fight like two rams, sometimes evenly matched and sometimes not; the weaker one gives way. So strive by every means, with skill and good application, so that today's effort quickly wins.
roles: Shows strive by every sound means.
yv.2.5.5.sa: द्वौ हुडाविव युध्येते पुरुषार्थौ समासमौ । प्राक्तनश्चैहिकश्चैव शाम्यत्यत्राल्पवीर्यवान् ॥ अतः पुरुषयत्नेन यतितव्यं यथा तथा । पुंसा तन्त्रेण सद्योगाद्येनाश्वद्यतनो जयेत् ॥

yv.2.6.18.m: Present effort overcomes the past, and the past can overpower the present. It is always a contest of human striving, and the one who stays calm wins.
yv.2.6.18.sa: ऐहिकः प्राक्तनं हन्ति प्राक्तनोऽद्यतनं बलात् । सर्वदा पुरुषस्पन्दस्तत्रानुद्वेगवाञ्जयी ॥

yv.2.6.2.m: As the effort, so quickly comes the fruit. So there is only effort; if you want to call it fate, it is that same effort.
roles: Shows results tied to effort, not a hidden decree.
yv.2.6.2.sa: यथा यथा प्रयत्नः स्याद्भवेदाशु फलं तथा । इति पौरुषमेवास्ति दैवमस्तु तदेव च ॥

yv.2.6.21.m: When wealth you built up step by step is lost, don't fall into despair. Where my strength has no power, what use is lamenting? If I grieved over what I cannot do, I should weep every day that I cannot stop death.
roles: Shows effort where it works and acceptance where it cannot.
yv.2.6.21.sa: क्रमेणोपार्जितेऽप्यर्थे नष्टे कार्या न खेदिता । न बलं यत्र मे शक्तं तत्र का परिदेवना ॥ यन्न शक्नोमि तस्यार्थे यदि दुःखं करोम्यहम् । तदमारितमृत्योर्मे युक्तं प्रत्यहरोदनम् ॥

yv.2.6.3.m: Just as in a painful moment people cry 'Oh, how painful!', so 'Oh, fate!' is only another way of saying the same thing.
roles: Names fate as a cry of pain, not an explanation.
yv.2.6.3.sa: दुःखाद्यथा दुःखकाले हा कष्टमिति कथ्यते । हाकष्टशब्दपर्यायस्तथा हा दैवमित्यपि ॥

yv.2.7.12.m: When the mind has sunk into bad things, bring it down into good ones with effort. That is the summary of all the scriptures.
roles: Turns the mind back each time.

yv.2.7.17.m: The one who eats is satisfied, not the one who doesn't; the one who walks arrives, not the one who stays put; the one who speaks is heard, not the silent one. Human effort bears fruit.
roles: Shows plain examples that doing is what works.
yv.2.7.17.sa: भोक्ता तृप्यति नाभोक्ता गन्ता गच्छति नागतिः । वक्ता वक्ति न चावक्ता पौरुषं सफलं नृणाम् ॥

yv.2.7.21.m: Results come from effort, sooner or later, depending on place and time. That arrival of the fruit, early or late, is what people call fate.
yv.2.7.21.sa: पुरुषार्थात्फलप्राप्तिर्देशकालवशादिह । प्राप्ता चिरेण शीघ्रं वा यासौ दैवमिति स्मृता ॥

yv.2.9.30.m: The river of our tendencies flows in two channels, good and bad. By your own effort, it must be steered into the good one.
roles: Shows choosing the channel again and again.
yv.2.9.30.sa: शुभाशुभाभ्यां मार्गाभ्यां वहन्ती वासनासरित् । पौरुषेण प्रयत्नेन योजनीया शुभे पथि ॥

yv.2.9.33.m: With evenness and gentle coaxing, not in a rush but little by little, by steady effort, look after the child that is your mind.
yv.2.9.33.sa: समता सांत्वनेनाशु न द्रागिति शनेशनेः । पौरुषेणैव यत्नेन पालयेच्चित्तबालकम् ॥

yv.2.9.39.m: Whatever one practises in the world, one becomes. This is seen without doubt in the wise, right from childhood.
roles: Shows practice is what shapes a person.
yv.2.9.39.sa: यद्यदभ्यस्यते लोके तन्मयेनैव भूयते । इत्याकुमारं प्राज्ञेषु दृष्टं संदेहवजितम् ॥

yv.3.16.24.m: O queen, by austerity, prayer and discipline every kind of attainment can be reached; but immortality is never gained.
roles: Shows the fear of a loved one's death meets a limit no effort removes.
yv.3.16.24.sa: तपोजपयमैर्देवि समस्ताः सिद्धसिद्धयः । संप्राप्यन्तेऽमरत्वं तु न कदाचन लभ्यते ॥

scene.s: Queen Lila loves her husband so much that she cannot bear the thought of his death. The wise tell her that nothing wins immortality, so she prays to the goddess Sarasvati instead. When the king dies, Sarasvati begins to show her that life and death are not what they seem.
scene.t: Queen Lila fears losing her husband

yv.3.16.50.m: Then Sarasvati, born of the sky, was moved with pity for her, utterly overwhelmed, as the first rain pities a little fish gasping in a drying pond.
roles: Shows help coming when one is overwhelmed.
yv.3.16.50.sa: अथ तामतिमात्रविह्वलां सकृपाकाशभवा सरस्वती । शफरीं ह्रदशोषविह्वलां प्रथमा वृष्टिरिवान्वकम्पत ॥

yv.5.10.9.m: Rise quickly, bless you, and do your appointed work. The great do not let the time slip by in their own duties.
yv.5.10.9.sa: शीघ्रमुत्तिष्ठ भद्रं ते नियतं कार्यमाचर । न कालमतिवर्तन्ते महान्तः स्वेषु कर्मसु ॥

yv.5.11.6.m: The more you casually spin up fancies and possibilities, the more your world of troubles swells, through your own worrying.
roles: Depicts the spinning of scenario after scenario.
yv.5.11.6.sa: यथा यथा विकल्पौघान्संकल्पयसि हेलया । तथा तथैति स्फारत्वं संसारस्तव चिन्तया ॥

yv.5.12.14.m: He does not chase the future or brood on the past; he simply goes along with the present moment, smiling.
roles: Shows a ruler at work and smiling.
yv.5.12.14.sa: भविष्यं नानुसंधत्ते नातीतं चिन्तयत्यसौ । वर्तमाननिमेषं तु हसन्नेवानुवर्तते ॥

yv.5.12.23.m: A wise person, even without help, sees a task through to its end; a person of poor judgment ruins even a great undertaking.
roles: Shows judgement counted as the decisive resource.
yv.5.12.23.sa: प्रज्ञावानसहायोऽपि कार्यान्तमधिगच्छति । दुष्प्रज्ञः कार्यमासाद्य प्रधानमपि नश्यति ॥

yv.5.12.26.m: The very effort people put into earning outer wealth should first be put into growing wisdom.
roles: Shows understanding placed first in the order of effort.
yv.5.12.26.sa: य एव यत्नः क्रियते बाह्यार्थोपार्जने जनैः । स एव यत्नः कर्तव्यः पूर्वं प्रज्ञाविवर्धने ॥

yv.5.21.10.m: When every means is blocked and even relatives have let go of your hand, nothing but your own courage lifts you out of the crisis.
roles: Shows one's own courage as the lifting hand.

yv.5.21.14.m: To a full mind, the whole world is filled with nectar; for one wearing shoes, the whole earth is as good as covered in leather.
roles: A full mind finds the world full.
yv.5.21.14.sa: पूर्णे मनसि संपूर्णं जगत्सर्वं सुधाद्रवैः । उपानद्रूढपादस्य ननु चर्मास्तृतैव भूः ॥

yv.5.21.6.m: Worry grows by thinking, as fire grows with fuel; and it dies by not being thought, as fire dies without fuel.
roles: Shows withholding fuel as a practice.
yv.5.21.6.sa: चिन्तनेनैधते चिन्ता त्विन्धनेनेव पावकः । नश्यत्यचिन्ततेनैव विनेन्धनमिवानलः ॥

yv.5.21.9.m: Taking discernment as your one true friend and wisdom as your seasoned companion, you can move through life and not lose your way in crises.
yv.5.21.9.sa: एकं विवेकं सुहृदमेकां प्रौढसखीं धियम् । आदाय विहरन्नेव संकटेषु न मुह्यति ॥

yv.5.24.19.m: This is extremely hard to attain and also easy, great-minded one: unpractised, it is very hard to reach; well practised, it comes easily.
roles: Practice makes the hard thing easy.
yv.5.24.19.sa: एषा ह्यत्यन्तदुष्प्रापा सुप्रापा च महामते । अनभ्यस्तातिदुष्प्रापा स्वभ्यस्ता प्राप्यते सुखम् ॥

scene.s: The demon king Bali has ruled the three worlds for ages. One day at his window he realises he is doing the same things day after day, night after night, and asks what any of it adds up to. He remembers a riddle his father Virochana once told him: a vast realm ruled by a silent king and an all-powerful minister. The minister is the mind; win it over, by practice, and everything is won.
scene.t: Bali tires of endless days and asks his father's riddle

yv.5.31.35.m: With all my being, all my mind, all the force of my striving: he alone, that God, is my refuge. There is no other way here.
roles: Gives refuge taken with one's whole being.
yv.5.31.35.sa: सर्वात्मना सर्वधिया सर्वसंरम्भरंहसा । स एव शरणं देवो गतिरस्तीह नान्यथा ॥

yv.5.31.37.m: From this very moment I take refuge, always, in Narayana, the unborn. Everywhere, I am full of Narayana.
yv.5.31.37.sa: अस्मान्निमेषादारभ्य नारायणमजं सदा । संप्रपन्नोऽस्मि सर्वत्र नारायणमयो ह्यहम् ॥

yv.5.31.38.m: The mantra 'Namo Narayanaya', which brings every aim to fulfilment, never leaves the chamber of my heart, as the wind never leaves the sky.
yv.5.31.38.sa: नमो नारायणायेति मन्त्रः सर्वार्थसाधकः । नापैति मम हृत्कोशादाकाशादिव मारुतः ॥

yv.5.33.19.m: Lovely treasure-house of the three worlds, remover of every stain, the highest light, refuge of those who have no refuge, the shelter-giving Lord: Hari, unborn, unfailing, the Lord, I take refuge in.
roles: Shows the act of taking refuge, spoken aloud.
yv.5.33.19.sa: त्रिभुवनभवनाभिरामकोशं सकलकलङ्कहरं परं प्रकाशम् । अशरणशरणं शरण्यमीशं हरिमजमच्युतमीश्वरं प्रपद्ये ॥

yv.5.36.1.m: The Self beyond every word has, after a long time, come back to memory. By good fortune you are found, Lord; salutations to you, great Self.
roles: Shows the gladness of finding it.
yv.5.36.1.sa: आत्मा सर्वपदातीतश्चिरात्संस्मृतिमागतः । दिष्ट्या लब्धोऽसि भगवन्नमस्तेस्तु महात्मने ॥

yv.5.41.3.m: Weighing what helps and what harms, and with hundreds of royal duties, I was utterly worn out, Lord. For a moment now, I have found rest.
roles: Shows a moment of rest is named and valued.
yv.5.41.3.sa: हिताहितविचारेण राजकार्यशतेन च । अत्यहं श्रमितो देव क्षणं विश्रामतां गतः ॥

yv.5.41.4.m: Lord, by your grace I have come to a rightly settled state. In meditation or out of it, I am always the same.
yv.5.41.4.sa: भगवंस्त्वत्प्रसादेन स्थितिः सम्यगथागता । समाधावसमाधौ च रूपेणाहं समः सदा ॥

yv.5.43.25.m: People lovingly make requests of Vishnu and the other gods; why not make the same loving appeal to your own mind?
yv.5.43.25.sa: क्रियते माधवादीनां प्रणयप्रार्थना स्वयम् । तथैव क्रियते कस्मान्न स्वकस्यैव चेतसः ॥

yv.5.43.32.m: Through daily practice and discernment the mind soon becomes clear, just as a mango slowly ripens into its sweetness.
roles: Shows daily practice, little by little.
yv.5.43.32.sa: नित्याभ्यासविवेकाभ्यां चित्तमाशु प्रसीदति । आम्र एव दशामेति साहकारीं शनैः शनैः ॥

yv.5.43.9.m: Sometimes the Self awakens on its own, by its own power; sometimes it is awakened through Vishnu, who is reached by devotion.
yv.5.43.9.sa: कदाचिदात्मनैवात्मा स्वयं शक्त्या प्रबुध्यते । कदाचिद्विष्णुदेहेन भक्तिलभ्येन बोध्यते ॥

yv.5.61.2.m: Holding to this way of seeing, the mind no longer burns with distress, like a child sunk in pitch darkness who has been given a lamp.
yv.5.61.2.sa: एतां दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य न मनः परितप्यते । घोरे तमसि निर्मग्नं लब्धदीपं शिशुर्यथा ॥

scene.s: After the story of King Suraghu, Vasishtha describes the relief of seeing clearly.

yv.5.64.33.m: Under the champak tree of a good person, whose leaves are tender, cooling words, with good shade and smiles for flowers, one rests at once, Rama, and deeply.
roles: Shows noticing the kind people one has.
yv.5.64.33.sa: स्निग्धशीतवचःपत्रे सच्छाये स्मितपुष्पके । क्षणाद्विश्रम्यते राम भृशं सुजनचम्पके ॥

yv.5.66.34.m: Carried along on endless great waves of tasks, the mind never gets a moment's rest; its depths dance with worry. 'This I've done, this I'm doing, this I'll do': so the bird of the mind, tangled in a net of reckonings, faints.
roles: Shows being caught in a net of done, doing, to do.
yv.5.66.34.sa: उह्यमानमनन्तेषु चेतः कार्यमहोर्मिषु । क्षणमेति न विश्रान्तिं चिन्ताताण्डविताशयम् ॥ इदं कृतं करोमीदं करिष्यामीदमित्यलम् । कलनाजालवलिता मूर्च्छिता मतिपक्षिणी ॥

yv.5.9.46.m: All those dazzling fortunes, if the mind clings to them, are really great calamities in grand disguise. And all those varied misfortunes, if the mind accepts them, are really fortunes.
roles: Shows the mind's stance deciding what an event becomes.
yv.5.9.46.sa: संपदश्च विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेच्चित्तेन संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा हन्त मन्ये महापदः ॥ आपदोऽपि विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेन्मनसि संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा मन्ये मनसि संपदः ॥

yv.5.9.59.m: 'I'm struck down, I'm ruined, I'm as good as dead': I have grieved this way again and again. What is gone is gone; now I will not keep weeping.
roles: A decision to stop the replay.
yv.5.9.59.sa: हा हतोऽस्मि विनष्टोऽस्मि मृतोऽस्मीति पुनःपुनः । शोचितं गतमेवाहमिदानीं नानुरोदिमि ॥

yv.6a.115.1.m: Be a great doer, a great enjoyer, and a great renouncer, sinless one, casting off all doubts and holding to lasting steadiness.
roles: Shows lasting steadiness as the base.
yv.6a.115.1.sa: महाकर्ता महाभोक्ता महात्यागी भवानघ । सर्वाः शङ्काः परित्यज्य धैर्यमालम्ब्य शाश्वतम् ॥

yv.6a.115.17.m: The thoughtful one who acts at the right time, with a mind unattached, doing what the task requires: that one is called a great doer.
yv.6a.115.17.sa: यथार्थकाले मतिमानसंसक्तमना मुनिः । कार्यानुरूपवृत्तस्थो महाकर्ता स उच्यते ॥

yv.6a.115.26.m: One who takes in great joys and sorrows evenly, as the ocean takes in the waters of rivers: that one is called a great enjoyer.
roles: Cultivates room enough for whatever arrives.
yv.6a.115.26.sa: महान्ति सुखदुःखानि यः पयांसीव सागरः । समं समुपगृह्णाति महाभोक्ता स उच्यते ॥

yv.6a.115.43.m: Staying turned inward while doing all the outer work that comes to you, you will never grow weary, and you will be free of the sense of being the doer.
roles: Shows acting without the claim of doership.
yv.6a.115.43.sa: अन्तर्मुखः सन्सततं समस्तं कुर्वन्बहिष्ठं खलु कार्यजातम् । न खेदमायासि कदाचिदेव निराकृताहंकृतितामुपैषि ॥

yv.6a.26.12.m: 'Today I got this; next I'll get that lovely thing': I have no such worry, and so I live long, free of illness.
yv.6a.26.12.sa: इदमद्य मया लब्धमिदं प्राप्स्यामि सुन्दरम् । इति चिन्ता न मे तेन चिरं जीवाम्यनामयः ॥

yv.6a.26.18.m: 'What has happened to me today? What will come tomorrow?' I have no such fever of worry; so I live long, free of illness.
yv.6a.26.18.sa: किमद्य मम संपन्नं प्रातर्वा भविता पुनः । इति चिन्ताज्वरो नास्ति तेन जीवाम्यनामयः ॥

yv.6a.26.28.m: Whenever I come to know something, sage, my mind does not turn arrogant; so I live long, free of illness.
yv.6a.26.28.sa: यदा यदा मुने किंचिद्विजानामि तदा तदा । मतिरायाति नौद्धत्यं तेन जीवाम्यनामयः ॥

yv.6a.26.34.m: I am happy when people are happy and sad when people are sad; I am a dear friend to all. So I live long, free of illness.
roles: Shows being pained with those in pain.
yv.6a.26.34.sa: सुखितोऽस्मि सुखापन्ने दुःखितो दुःखिते जने । सर्वस्य प्रियमित्रं च तेन जीवाम्यनामयः ॥

yv.6a.26.8.m: I never brood over the past or the future. I hold my attention on the present, here, with myself.
roles: Names a long life lived lightly.
yv.6a.26.8.sa: न भूतं न भविष्यं च चिन्तयामि कदाचन । दृष्टिमालम्ब्य तिष्ठामि वर्तमानामिहात्मना ॥

yv.6a.29.108.m: For those whose minds whirl in the joy of remembering you, nothing is hard to reach, and there are no fears at all.
yv.6a.29.108.sa: न किंचिदपि दुष्प्रापं न च काश्चन भीतयः । त्वदनुस्मरणानन्दपरिघूर्णितचेतसाम् ॥

yv.6a.29.111.m: Remembering you, Lord, sows the seed of what is to come; it is the one jar of wisdom's nectar, a moon shining with steadiness. Remembering you, Lord, is the door to the city of freedom. Holding the great wish-jewel of remembering you, I...
roles: It is called a moon of steadiness.
yv.6a.29.111.sa: तनोति चैष्यतो बीजं त्वदनुस्मरणं प्रभो । ज्ञानामृतैककलशो धृतिज्योत्स्नानिशाकरः ॥ अपवर्गपुरद्वारं त्वदनुस्मरणं प्रभो । त्वदनुस्मरणोदारचिन्तामणिमता मया ॥

yv.6a.39.2.m: Whether walking or standing, awake or asleep, this worship runs through every activity, always: it is worship made of meditation.
roles: Shows practice carried inside ordinary activity.
yv.6a.39.2.sa: गच्छतस्तिष्ठतश्चैव जाग्रतः स्वपतोऽपि च । सर्वाचारगता पूजा नित्यं ध्यानात्मिका त्वियम् ॥

yv.6a.93.29.m: Good man, true renunciation does not come from giving up the body, nor from giving up the kingdom, nor from wasting away in a hut, O king.
yv.6a.93.29.sa: साधो न देहत्यागेन न राज्यत्यजनेन च । न चोटजादिशोषेण सर्वत्यागो भवेन्नृप ॥

yv.6a.93.43.m: Those who know renunciation say that giving up the clinging mind is giving up everything. When that is achieved, great one, what truth is not experienced?
roles: Shows truth when the mind's grip ends.
yv.6a.93.43.sa: चित्तत्यागं विदुः सर्वत्यागं त्यागविदां वर । तस्मिन्सिद्धे महाबाहो सत्यं किं नानुभूयते ॥

yv.6b.44.32.m: In its shade the deer of the mind, tired out along the way, rests: a traveller worn out since birth on a road full of noise.
roles: Depicts a mind tired since birth by noise and travel.
yv.6b.44.32.sa: यस्यामवान्तरश्रान्तो विश्राम्यति मनोमृगः । आजन्मजीर्णपथिकः पथि कोलाहलाकुलः ॥

scene.s: Vasishtha describes the cool shade of the tree of understanding.
